transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington on Korva Coleman, Israel is marking three years since
Hamas launched the October 7th attacks.
Memorials are being held throughout Israel to the nearly 1,200 victims of those attacks.
NPR's Daniel Estrin reports from a memorial site in southern Israel.
This is the site of the deadliest single attack of October 7th, three years ago, the Nova
Music Festival, where more than 400 people were killed.
Families are dusting off small memorial plaques.
Orit Barone's daughter was killed here.
I'm very angry about everybody, God, all the politicians.
We will find out on the 27th of October what will happen.
That is the date Israel holds national elections.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is seeking a new term.
Today, protesters gathered outside his home.
They're angry he's refused to launch an official national investigation into the security failure
of October 7th.
Daniel Estrin, NPR News, the Nova Festival memorial near the Gaza border.
The day after the Hamas-led attack, Israel began the war in Gaza.
Officials in Gaza say Israeli attacks have killed more than 74,000 Palestinians.
Germany is shocked over spying allegations against the former head of the country's
intelligence agency, Esmee Nicholson reports from Berlin.
Let's be clear about the magnitude of these allegations.
August Haning served as the head of Germany's CIA equivalent, known here as the BND, for
seven years.
Federal prosecutors accused Haning of using classified information to brief a foreign
intelligence agency in at least one instance.
That amounts to attempted treason.
Researchers also believe that Haning was in close contact with a member of another foreign
intelligence agency, to whom he passed sensitive political information.
Esmee Nicholson reporting.
NPR has learned that FBI teams that track foreign spies have been hit with deep cuts
around the country.
That's even as the U.S. remains mired in the Iran war and tense geopolitical rivalries with
China and Russia.
NPR's Ryan Lucas has the exclusive reporting.
The cuts to FBI counterintelligence squads are so significant that in some of the bureau's
field offices, they only have 50 to 60 percent of positions filled.
And in some field offices, the number of counterintelligence squads has been reduced by half.
That's according to five people familiar with the matter who spoke on condition of anonymity
out of fear of retribution.
One source called the cuts terrifying in light of the growing threats.
The staff reductions are a ripple effect of Director Kash Patel's focus on violent crime
and immigration enforcement.
Agents and analysts are being pulled off of hunting foreign spies and instead put on violent
crime or immigration work.
In response to questions, the FBI says it maintains a robust counterintelligence effort.
Ryan Lucas, NPR News, Washington.
You're listening to NPR.
President Trump will fly to Texas today to attend a political rally in San Antonio.
He'll be there to stump with Republican candidates, including U.S. Senate candidate Ken Paxton.
Another candidate who will join them is congressional candidate Carlos de la Cruz.
Trump has been to Texas three times in less than a month.
Parts of Louisiana, Alabama, and the Florida panhandle could see effects from a tropical
system forecast to gain strength later this week.
Tropical storm Isaias is moving through the southern Gulf of Mexico with sustained winds
of 40 miles per hour.
As NBA's Matt Blume reports, it could strengthen to become the first hurricane of the Atlantic
season.
The National Hurricane Center says there's an increasing risk of dangerous winds and storm
surge for parts of the Gulf late Friday into Saturday this week.
It's still early, but Florida Governor Ron DeSantis declared a preliminary state of emergency
in 25 counties, while BP, Shell, and Chevron have evacuated some staff from offshore rigs.
A strong wind shear in the Gulf has helped limit storms this season, but water temperatures
remain high, which is expected to help rapidly strengthen this system as it moves north.
Matt Blume, NPR News, New Orleans.
This year's Nobel Prize in Chemistry has been awarded to two scientists for their work
on mirror images in molecules.
Henri B. Kagan and Kenzo Soai have discovered ways to show mirror images in chemical reactions.
This has been critical for scientists working to create new medications.
This is NPR.
